chunks: Ja'far, from Anbasah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Beware of the mention of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them), for there is nothing more hateful to them than the mention of Ali and Fatima (peace be upon them).
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by 'beware of the mention of Ali and Fatima'?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq warns believers to be wary of the 'mention' (dhikr) of Imam Ali and Fatima, noting that for the general populace—particularly the hypocrites (munafiqun) and enemies of the Ahl al-Bayt—there is nothing more detestable than hearing about them. This highlights the deep emotional and spiritual connection the Ahl al-Bayt have with their followers and the aversion of their enemies. The phrase 'dhikr' here can refer to both the act of remembering them and the public proclamation of their status, serving as a test of sincerity for the masses.

en.hubeali: H 14604 – Ja’far, from Anbasat, from Abu Abdullahasws having said:
‘Beware of mentioning Aliasws and Fatimaasws (in front of others) for there is nothing more hateful to them than the speaking of Aliasws and Fatimaasws’.
en.sarwar: 156. Ja’far, from Anbasat, from Abu Abdullah (a.s.) having said:
‘Beware of mentioning Ali (a.s.) and Fatima (a.s.) (in front of others) for there is nothing more hateful to them than the speaking of Ali (a.s.) and Fatima (a.s.)’.
